reasoning: Corn stalks showing distinctive shiny dark black/blue-black discoloration on the external rind surface, forming large blotches and streaks across multiple internodes. This is the hallmark diagnostic feature of anthracnose stalk rot. Other stalk rots were ruled out: bacterial stalk rot shows soft slimy rot with collapse, charcoal stalk rot shows internal shredded pith with tiny sclerotia, Diplodia shows dry tan stalks with small pycnidia, and Physoderma stalk rot shows black nodes specifically at the first/second node.
